regions.evidence: Satellite (spring 2021, after the 2020-11 window): continuous grey asphalt from just beyond the crosswalk. On the left is the kerb of a raised median island with a bench/shelter structure and planters at its rounded nose; r1's left edge follows that kerb and the nose curve. On the right is the left line of a hatched painted buffer. Cross-section profiles on the sunlit part show no lane line inside r1 between the island kerb and the buffer line: one wide general-traffic lane, roughly 4.5-5 m (scale estimated from vehicle length). The upper ~35% lies in building shadow; the island kerb line and the pavement continue there. Street views (2020-11, in the window): at 34.6 m the away view shows the camera in a single wide WB lane between a yellow edge line along the raised grass median with trees and a hatched buffer with white flexible posts. The 34.6 m toward view shows the same single lane back to the crosswalk. At 54.1 m the lane continues as one lane where the median jogs (S-bend). Matched by physical sequence (median kerb, lane, hatched buffer, bike lane, kerb), not by ordinal. The 104 m views show a wider multi-lane cross-section with dashed lines, beyond this polygon; they do not change r1's single-lane reading near the junction.

visual_refs.finding: unmarked asphalt with no internal lane line
kerb of the raised median island forming r1's left edge
single WB travel lane between yellow edge line and hatched buffer
raised grass median with trees and yellow edge line on the left

regions.evidence: Satellite: a narrow strip (about 1 m) between two parallel solid white lines, with diagonal hatch bars painted between them at regular intervals along its whole length. This is a painted buffer, not a travel facility. Street views (2020-11): at 34.6 m (away and toward) the same two-line buffer with diagonal hatching carries white flexible delineator posts and separates the travel lane from the kerbside bicycle lane.

visual_refs.finding: two solid white lines with diagonal hatch bars
hatched buffer with white flexible delineator posts
same hatched buffer seen looking back toward the junction

regions.evidence: Satellite: a paved strip (about 1.7-1.9 m) between the buffer's right line and the kerb. Beyond the kerb are a light sidewalk with a row of round reddish planters, granite-edged tree pits and further sidewalk. Inside the strip near the junction is a bicycle-lane glyph with a straight arrow ahead of it pointing in the WB travel direction. The arrow is a bike-lane direction marking, not a motor turn arrow. Street views (2020-11): at 34.6 m the strip beyond the post-lined buffer runs along the kerb, with parked bikes and a sidewalk beyond. At 54.1 m the kerbside lane continues with green paint and bicycle markings. The width, buffer and markings fit a buffered bicycle lane; it is too narrow for a car lane.

visual_refs.finding: bicycle glyph and straight direction arrow inside the strip
kerb, then sidewalk with round planters immediately right of the strip
kerbside bicycle lane beyond the post-lined buffer
green-painted bicycle lane continuing along the kerb

notes: All six street views are 2020-11, inside the target window, from three panoramas (34.6, 54.1, 104.0 m); the away/toward pairs are not independent. The satellite is spring 2021, later context; it agrees with the street views on all three regions.
The cameras are on the WB carriageway itself (median on the left looking away, kerb and bike lane on the right), so no across-median correspondence was needed.

An orange temporary lane-shift warning sign stands on the right sidewalk in the 34.6 m away view. Lane positions may have been temporarily altered at that time, though the paint seen matches the satellite.
Downstream (104 m) the carriageway widens to several lanes with dashed lines; that lies beyond these candidate regions.
